# Pandamonium v1.0.56

This patch removes the protocol toggle panel from Settings and adds tailnet model discovery: any node on the operator's tailnet can now be scanned, probed, and registered as a model endpoint directly from Add Models. It also lands real, bound chat projects, a docked message queue, and the docked-modal freeze fix from the parallel workspace lanes.

## MAD-920 — Projects: make chat projects real, bound, and part of Chats

### Problem

Projects appeared in two places. The sidebar had a standalone Projects section for real workstation directories (MAD-902), while the Chats list rendered a second "Projects" group built from free-form `session.folder` strings written by the manual Move-to-folder menu and the AI tidy pass. Those chat projects were not real records and were not bound anywhere, so the same idea was presented twice and neither surface was the source of truth. Leo's review: projects are meant to organize sessions, and a project is a real folder stamped with the WhoAmI build.

### Implementation

Projects now live inside Chats and are backed by the project registry. `sessions.project_id` is added as an additive SQLite column (`core/database.py`) and returned by `/api/sessions`; session creation and `PATCH /api/session/{id}` accept a validated project binding, and removing a project unbinds its chats without deleting them. A one-time idempotent startup migration (`src/project_registry.migrate_session_folders`, run from `app.py`) converts every distinct legacy folder name into a project and binds its sessions, excluding the system `Tasks` and `Assistant` groupings. New projects are scaffolded with the WhoAmI project-local starter (`src/whoami_project_template`, project-local-ai-growth v1.0.0) — AGENTS.md, STATUS.md, HANDOVER.md, MEMORY.md, BUGS.md, SYSTEM-MAP.md, DECISIONS.md, BACKLOG.md, IMPORT.md, tickets/, evidence/, and artifacts/ — with `AI-GROWTH-WORKSPACE` replaced by the project name; existing files are never overwritten and imported folders are left untouched. The sidebar (`static/js/sessions.js`, `static/js/projects.js`) renders the Projects group and its folders from the registry, gives each project a hover `+` that starts a session bound to it, moves the create/import menu onto the Projects header, and replaces Move to folder with Move to project. The AI tidy pass now assigns chats to existing projects only and never invents one. Session and project move handles are invisible at rest and appear on row hover, focus-within, or `body.rearrange-mode`, matching the section headers from MAD-908; touch layouts keep them available.

### Product value and UI visibility

There is now one Projects surface, inside Chats: create/import a project, see its chats grouped under it, start a session in it, and move chats between projects. Creating a project produces a real folder carrying the WhoAmI project build, so agent sessions start from a correct project-local operating contract. The standalone Projects sidebar section is gone, the fake chat folders are converted into real projects, and the move handles no longer clutter every chat and project row.

### Verification

Full Python suite: 5,772 passed, 5 skipped. Full browser suite: 109 passed (chromium, workers=1), including the updated `mad-902-projects`, `mad-820-sidebar-organization`, `session-ordering`, and `m7-codex-workspace` specs. New `tests/test_projects_in_chats.py` covers scaffolding and no-overwrite behavior, imported folders not being scaffolded, migration conversion with `Tasks`/`Assistant` exclusions and idempotency, unbinding on project removal, route-level validation and PATCH binding/clearing, list projection of `project_id`, and frontend source guards for the removed section and hidden handles. PR #153 CI is green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependencies. The database change is additive and the migration is idempotent and never deletes data; project removal never deletes a folder or a chat. The migration creates real directories under `DATA_DIR/projects` on first start, as approved for converting the existing chat folders. Project order now stores project ids under the existing `sidebar-project-order` preference, so a previously saved folder-name order is ignored until reordered. Projects are installation-wide and appear in every agent view. The WhoAmI starter is baked in at v1.0.0; a future v1.1.0 bake-in is separate work.

## MAD-928 — Settings: remove the Protocols panel and raw model-window/budget editors

### Problem

Settings → AI Defaults presented the JOS protocol layer as an operator toggle even though protocol packs mount by design, and it exposed raw JSON editors for model context windows and input token budgets that were unusable in normal operation. Both surfaces invited settings changes that the runtime did not honor the way the UI implied.

### Implementation

Removes the Protocols card from Settings → AI Defaults, including the "Mount the protocol layer" toggle, the JOS-IPAV and JOS-P0–P7 pack checkboxes, the Model context windows and Model input token budgets JSON editors, and the card's save action. `static/js/settings.js` no longer defines or calls `initProtocolSettings()`, and Settings neither reads nor posts protocol settings keys. Agent Identity and Default Chat Model cards are unchanged. Runtime protocol mounting, `/api/diagnostics/protocol/packs`, and discovery-driven context windows and budgets are untouched.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings no longer offers controls that do not match the product contract, and the unusable raw JSON editors are gone. Protocols keep mounting automatically and runtime behavior is unchanged.

### Verification

New `protocol-settings-removed.spec.js` browser check asserts the panel, toggle, pack list, and both JSON editors are absent, that Settings fires no `/api/diagnostics/protocol/packs` request, and that the Agent Identity and model-default cards still render; `protocol-settings.spec.js` is removed with the panel. New `tests/test_protocol_settings_removed.py` source guard passes. MAD-784/890–893 protocol tests remain green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

UI removal only; no dependency, API, schema, or runtime behavior change. Any previously saved protocol settings keys are simply no longer edited from Settings.

### References

- [Linear MAD-928](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-928)

## MAD-933 — Models: add tailnet scan and "Add Tailscale Models" to Add Models

### Problem

"Scan Models" only probed local ports; the bounded tailnet discovery API existed but the Settings UI never called it, and there was no operator-facing way to register a model server running on another tailnet node. Worker/agent connectivity was hardcoded, so a normal user could not connect their own nodes.

### Implementation

Added an "Add Tailscale Models" card to Settings → Add Models. Scan Tailnet lists online peers through the existing bounded discovery API (opaque peer ids and OS only, 120s TTL, up to 5 selected); the operator selects peers, probes them, and each finding registers through `POST /api/model-endpoints` with `endpoint_kind=tailnet`. The browser never receives peer addresses: the new `resolve_tailnet_candidate` resolves the address server-side from the issued peer selection and returns the base URL only to the registration path. Ollama candidates register at the root URL; OpenAI-compatible candidates at `/v1`. Manual tailnet URL entry is the fallback, and Added Models now groups endpoints into Local / API / Tailnet. Tailnet endpoints use local-class refresh intervals and timeouts.

### Product value and UI visibility

Any tailnet node running a model server can be connected from Settings without an agent's help. Tailnet endpoints appear under Added Models → Tailnet with their model counts, and their models show up in the composer picker like any other endpoint.

### Verification

`tests/test_safe_tailnet_discovery.py` covers probe-free/redacted peer listing, probe candidates exposing port but not address, server-side base URL resolution for OpenAI-compatible and Ollama targets, and TTL/unknown-port rejection. `tests/test_model_routes.py` covers tailnet kind classification, server-side resolution during create, and 400s for incomplete or unissued selections. `tests/browser/tailnet-models.spec.js` drives scan → select → probe → per-row add and the manual URL path. Focused Python set: 240 passed; browser: 2 passed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Additive: `tailnet` is a new endpoint kind and existing endpoints keep their Local/API grouping. Peer addresses stay server-side and are not returned by discovery responses. The 5-peer selection limit, peer-id TTL, and bounded probe behavior are reused unchanged. Agent endpoints and SSH connections remain future M16 slices.

### References

- [Linear MAD-933](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-933/models-add-tailnet-scan-and-add-tailscale-models-to-add-models)

## MAD-942 — UI: stop the modal z-stack observer from freezing the renderer

### Problem

When a side-docked tool (for example the Pandamonium Updater) was already open, clicking Settings, the profile button, or another sidebar tool froze the renderer until Chrome killed the tab.

### Implementation

The global modal z-stack observer in `static/js/ui.js` promoted every class and style mutation on a visible `.modal`. Because `_promote` writes an inline z-index, that write re-fired the same observer; with two visible modals each batch raised one above the other forever in a microtask loop (`_zCounter` climbed 1000 → 2028). Promotion now happens on visibility transitions only: each modal's last visible state is tracked in a `WeakMap`, and cosmetic writes on an already-visible modal no longer trigger promotion. "Most recently opened wins" is preserved.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings, the profile menu, and sidebar tools open normally while another docked tool is visible; the renderer no longer locks up.

### Verification

New `tests/browser/mad-942-dock-freeze.spec.js`: 3 passed, and the same tests fail with the pre-fix `ui.js`. Existing `modal-lifecycle.spec.js` plus `mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js`: 31 passed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend z-order logic only; no API, schema, or data change. Ships from the parallel workspace lane (PR #163).

### References

- [Linear MAD-942](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-942/ui-stop-modal-z-stack-observer-from-freezing-the-renderer)

## MAD-943 — Chat: dock queued messages above the composer

### Problem

Queued messages rendered as a chat bubble inside the conversation history, mixing pending sends with the conversation and offering no Steer, Edit, or Delete.

### Implementation

Queued messages now render as compact cards in `#chat-queue-strip` inside `.chat-input-bar`, docked above the composer and out of `#chat-history`. Each card shows the queue icon, truncated text, Steer, and a "..." menu with inline Edit (Enter saves, Escape cancels) and Delete. Steer reuses the existing promote path (stop the active response, send that item now); multiple items stack FIFO and the stream-end drain removes each card as it sends. The old queued-bubble styles and queue toast were removed.

### Product value and UI visibility

Pending messages stay visible directly above the composer without polluting chat history, and operators can steer, edit, or delete them before they send.

### Verification

New `tests/browser/chat-queue.spec.js`: 4 passed. `node --check` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only. True mid-turn injection into the running model turn and queue persistence across reload are out of scope for this slice. Ships from the parallel workspace lane (PR #166).
